text: When my dad was still alive we would play this game day after day building base after base across the map and finding story piece after story piece, and falling in love with willow and hoops' entertaining banter with eachother as we played , and though we never got to finish the story together this game still created countless fond memories, would highly recommend for groups or familys <3
This game is the Dark Souls of my dad coming into the room with a belt.

I never played a Silent Hill game before. I bought this one because everyone talks about how SH2 is incredible and all that. I played it a few hours and didn't get it.

Fast forward a few weeks, I am talking to a stranger at the local bar. Somehow we get to talking about SH2. He is a big fan. I tell him my struggles getting into the game. He told me to just go back and play it. "Just play it man." Okay, so I played the game.

Damn. I get it now. I have even gone back to play the first game, third game, PSP spinoffs, etc.
Great stuff. This is a game that will stick with you.

The game is absolutely beautiful and the sound design/music is very well done, however that's about all I enjoyed about it. The platforming and puzzles are both pretty boring IMO. There is little to no challenge anywhere to be found in the first hour of playing. All puzzles are pretty much "direct your cute companion to stand here and/or perform this action so you can move to the next spot."

I would say it's a good game for someone not looking for a challenge and just wants to enjoy the world, but that's about it.

I absolutely loved every aspect of this game. 

It’s been a while since a game made me feel this genuinely wholesome and happy. It reminded me to appreciate the little things in life, the people around me, and most importantly, the friends who make everything better.

I’m so glad I played this. Thank you to everyone who made this game — it’s something I’ll remember for a long time.

A cut above the rest in the friend-slop era. Minigames are well-made and challenging, super fun & funny to figure out and realize what information you have to give and what your friends can't see/hear/share. My only criticism is that some puzzles are nearly impossible to solve on the first attempt (symbol spinner, Morse code, Simon says). Would still absolutely recommend though, a much better game than most others releasing in this genre.

Thank you, UNO, for forever changing my life for the better

Pros:
-A lot of replayability, with multiple endings and paths.
-Graphics are really nice, pixel art with retro style.
-Simple gameplay
-Price

Cons:
-Off-game interface.
-If I kill my sister using a mirror shard, why don't I end up with blood all over my hands? The game should have a bathroom and take those things into account

Suggestions:
-Characters portraits seem to be pre rendered from a 3D object. It would be more consistent if it was more pixelated, at least.
-It would be better to be able to interact with more objects and weapons.
-Reposition the characters and items, and change the story slightly between different playthroughs.

Overall, the game is a really good experience that for the price is really worth it.

Old Blood is essentially a loose retelling of Return to Castle Wolfenstein, but in the universe and style of The New Order. Its basically just a big expansion, but it operates at the same quality as New Order. Its really fun seeing some of the old RTCW ideas revisited, and getting to see more of the WW2 stuff you only see briefly in New Order. Also, it runs much better!

Dave the Diver is one of the quintessential games to highlight that you don't need $100M and insane graphical fidelity to make a game great. Hitting the 2D artstyle niche, addictive gameplay loop, and surprisingly well done story about the fictional supernatural aspects of ocean life, while trying to run a sushi shop, makes this game something that a lot of AAA publishers seem to forget on what a video game should sometimes be. FUN, ESCAPISM, and VIBES

Resident Evil 4 is one of those games that constantly keeps things fresh. Every new area, enemy type and encounter gives you something different to deal with.

Leon is an absolute MVP. Luis is the kind of bro you'd actually want watching your back.

The pacing is excellent. It knows exactly when to slow things down, when to throw a horde at you and when to make you question your life choices.

Honorable mention to the bella sisters… Apparently one homicidal maniac with a chainsaw wasn't enough.

The game looks fantastic, runs flawlessly and didn't crash once.

Absolutely worth playing.

This game is like waking up in a Soviet utopia, only to be chased by robots gone rogue and yelled at by your talking glove who thinks it's smarter than you (it is).
The plot is chaotic, confusing, and completely unhinged, just like Mother Russia intended.
It’s like BioShock got drunk on vodka, punched Cyberpunk in the face, and then tried to juggle philosophy, communism, and slapstick horror - all while ballet dancing on hardbass.
Thus, BLYATPUNK !!

Huge gameplay improvements over the first one, which was already incredible. Now I find it hard to go back to the first game just because the combat in Hades II feels so smooth. As always, great story and voice acting, with lots of it, and a love letter to fans of Greek myth. There's not much else to say when a game is this good.

Wonderful horror short-form game with, frankly, some infuriating game design decisions and some of the worst platforming that I've played in recent years. Honestly, final hour (out of 5) was almost unbearable because of cheap deaths and unresponsive boss segments. 

Ending segment timings are so brutal they've felt more like cyberpsort than atmospheric storytelling. And I've platinumed Astro Bot just recently so it's not like I don't know how to play platformers.

Still, quite woth it IMO. It's an imaginative and very eerie little story with impeccable art design and very moody soundtrack. And it's still lingering in my mind after the ending credits rolled, so it's definetly successful at leaving some mark on people.

After playing the entire game pretty casually, collecting stuff as it comes and soaking in the story and such, I replayed it while  exploring as much as I could, the many nooks and crannies and new movement mechanics enticed me greatly. I now Find myself replaying it a third time as carefully and thoroughly as I can. Turns out, I missed quite a bit even when I was trying, and the giddy sensation I get when stumbling onto a small, seemingly insignificant crevice, only to find a tiny piece of the world is exhilarating. The art direction is truly wonderful and effective, and the simple yet effective gameplay gives you just enough mental space to soak in the atmosphere, even during a line. I'd say it's entirely worth the price!
